clue.text: Cat losing seconds repeatedly chasing shy rodent

indicators.note: losing means dropping, and repeatedly says the word seconds stands for more than one letter to remove

blocks.note: coy means bashful or shy
puss is a familiar word for a cat
S is the standard abbreviation for seconds, removed twice here

explanation.surface: A cat keeps losing ground as it chases a timid rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' places the shortened cat after the shy word; both of its seconds are removed, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Note girl is after hairstyle that's refined

blocks.note: a cut is a haircut, a hairstyle
G is a musical note
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A note says a girl wants a smart, sophisticated hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is after' sends the note and girl behind the hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a very precise, upper-class British way of speaking, hence refined.

clue.text: Rhea, perhaps under three feet, captive in the US

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below, so the bird comes second after the measure

blocks.note: a yard is three feet
a rhea is a large flightless bird, an example of a bird

explanation.surface: A rhea, held in a pen about a yard high, in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places the bird below the yard in this down answer. Bird is also British slang for prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardbird is American slang for a convict, someone held in a prison yard.

clue.text: Cube confused with exponential? Unlikely to be called out

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A maths student mixing up cubes and exponentials will hardly be praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called out' looks like singling out for praise; it means objected to, as in calling out bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexceptionable gives no grounds for objection, so nobody would challenge it.

clue.text: Plan to squander and run off

blocks.note: to blue money is old slang for spending it recklessly
to run off copies is to print them

explanation.surface: Someone's scheme is to waste the money and then flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' suggests escaping, but here it means producing copies on a press. To blue (or blow) money is British slang for squandering it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed technical drawing, hence any detailed scheme or design.

clue.text: Float to purchase a container for oxygen

indicators.note: a container holds something, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: to buy is to purchase
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An instruction for a diver to buy an oxygen tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Float' is the noun, a moored marker on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is an anchored float marking a channel or hazard at sea.

clue.text: Odd time almost completely quiet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: odd numbers are uneven
T is the abbreviation for time
full means complete, as in full well

explanation.surface: A strange period that was nearly totally silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneventful day is one where nothing happens, so it is quiet.

clue.text: Film a sheep running under tree on old homestead

indicators.note: running suggests moving about freely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the plane is a tree, common in London streets
toft is an archaic word for a homestead
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheep runs loose under a tree on an old farmstead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs with 'homestead': TOFT is a dated word. In this down answer the tree sits on the homestead and the jumbled sheep comes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Planet of the Apes is the 1968 science-fiction film and its sequels and remakes.

clue.text: Know instinctively northern dweller accepts temperature

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Inuit live in the Arctic regions
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: An Arctic native senses the cold without being told.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to grasp it by instinct rather than reasoning.

clue.text: Seat of power good for European crowd

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter is swapped in where the other was

blocks.note: a throne is a monarch's seat
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A seat of government benefits the people of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: G replaces the E at the end of THRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large, densely packed crowd of people.

clue.text: Home with trees arranged in small group

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house surrounded by trees planted in a small cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a set of three people or things, a very small group.

clue.text: Atmosphere about street is bustling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: air is the atmosphere around us
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: The mood on a city street is busy and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and moving about, in a state of activity, as bustling does.

clue.text: Live with success around German city

indicators.note: around means one word is placed so it surrounds the other

blocks.note: luck means good fortune or success
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a prosperous life in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lübeck is a Hanseatic port city in northern Germany, famous for marzipan.

clue.text: Change the appearance of flag, not new

indicators.note: not tells us to leave something out of the word before

blocks.note: the Red Ensign is the flag of the British merchant navy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An instruction to restyle a flag, but not with something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign, the 'red duster', flies on British merchant ships; dropping its N gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign something is to alter its form or look, so it changes the appearance of it.

clue.text: British worker embracing to some extent chaps in exile

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping arms around, so the word holds the others inside

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a worker ant; ant is the crossword's usual worker
-ish, also used alone, means somewhat or to some extent
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A British labourer welcomes some fellow expatriates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' is a definition of the informal suffix -ish, not an indicator for a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment is being expelled from one's country, which is the same state as exile.

clue.text: Dismantle vehicle for the purpose of working a series of panels

blocks.note: to strip an engine is to take it apart
a car is a vehicle
as in 'in order to'
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Taking a car apart to get at its body panels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panels' looks like car bodywork; it is the frames of a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip cartoon is a sequence of drawings in boxes telling a story, such as a newspaper comic strip.

clue.text: Lead with buffet covered in fruit

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a grape is a fruit
to buffet is to strike or hit

explanation.surface: Someone heads to a buffet laden with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it is the verb, to strike. 'Lead' is the pencil sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Pencil 'lead' is in fact graphite, a soft form of carbon.

clue.text: Division of church in ten parts roughly

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters are set out loosely in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church split into roughly ten sections.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, a distinct part of the building.

clue.text: Brief result I brought about? Far from it

definitions.text: Brief result I brought about? Far from it

indicators.note: brought about suggests turning things round, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker denies having produced a quick outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a speaker who talks on endlessly to block a vote achieves the very opposite of a brief result.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibusterer delays legislation with extremely long speeches, so a quick outcome is the last thing they create.

clue.text: Mexican, note, cross with detective

blocks.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
X is a cross
tec is slang for detective; with adds it on

explanation.surface: A Mexican, according to a note, is angry with a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the X shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mixtec are an indigenous people of southern Mexico, so a Mixtec is a Mexican.

clue.text: Adviser to Charlemagne Gauls caution regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An adviser to the Frankish emperor warns the Gauls.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are kept, starting with the A of Gauls.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcuin of York was an eighth-century scholar who led Charlemagne's palace school and advised him.

clue.text: Victorian work is old anthem entirely unfinished

indicators.note: every word is left without its ending, so each one loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A Victorian piece of music turns out to be an old anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entirely' means all three words lose their last letter, not just the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is an 1882 comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, a work of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Perhaps dredge river in front of submarine dock

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pen is a sheltered dock for submarines

explanation.surface: Clearing silt from a river to make room for a submarine base.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland. The definition is a verb: dredging is one way to make water deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging scoops material from a channel bed, an example of making water deeper.

clue.text: Kitty's daughter chasing light-hearted pleasure

blocks.note: fun is light-hearted enjoyment
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Kitty's girl is out looking for a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a name; it is a pool of money. 'Chasing' puts D after FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pot of money, which is a fund.

clue.text: Something that may give one a lift from doctor on Thursday

definitions.text: Something that may give one a lift

blocks.note: Thu is the short form of Thursday
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient gets a boost from a doctor's Thursday visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the doctor after Thursday in an across answer. The definition points to hitchhiking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker sticks out a thumb to ask passing drivers for a ride, so it may get one a lift.

clue.text: Balance arm is caught in edges of one

indicators.note: something caught in is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
the first and last letters of one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gymnast's balance depends on arm position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a verb here: to supply with weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is an equal distribution of weight or force, a state of balance.

clue.text: At one time included, quoted in vain

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to cite is to quote
once means at one time in the past

explanation.surface: Someone once named in a list proved to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In vain' reads as a phrase; 'in' belongs with 'quoted' and 'vain' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person is excessively proud of themselves, which is what vain means.

clue.text: Delightful one for the king in lodge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a set is a badger's burrow or lodge
a monarch uses the royal we where others would say one or I

explanation.surface: A lovely room set aside for the king at a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we' is the king's word for himself; it goes inside SET, a badger's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means pleasing or charming, a common synonym for delightful.
